questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why so many people like looking at pictures of cats online
How the World Wide Web was built
Tim Berners-Lee's worries about the internet
questions.why: They discuss Berners-Lee's concerns about the internet and his suggestions for changing it.

questions.q: What did Neil first use the internet for?
questions.why: Neil says 'I looked up pictures of cats!'

questions.q: What does Neil say about living without the internet?
options: It would be possible, but much less convenient
He has already tried living without it for a whole year
questions.why: Neil says 'Not impossible, but not nearly as convenient.'

questions.q: What did Tim Berners-Lee first think internet giants needed to do?
options: Just be neutral and let people connect
Charge people to use the internet
questions.why: He says initially he felt they just had to be neutral, just be a platform.

questions.q: Which website does Berners-Lee give as a good example of connecting people?
questions.why: He says if you connect humanity via Wikipedia, they produce wonderful things in general.

questions.q: According to Berners-Lee, why can social networks bring out the worst in people?
options: People can hide who they really are
People spend far too long on them every day
questions.why: He says when people have anonymity, 'it can bring out the very nastiest of people'.

questions.q: How does Berners-Lee suggest social networks could improve things?
options: By banning retweets and shares on all social networks
By giving more kudos for being constructive
By making people pay for accounts
questions.why: He suggests changing the way people get kudos, 'give them more kudos for being constructive'.

questions.q: What question does Rob raise about Berners-Lee's suggestion?
options: Who would decide what is constructive
Whether people would stop using the internet
questions.why: Rob says 'I wonder who would decide if something is constructive?'
